cohort: The study included 17,994 adult mothers (15,448 aged 20-34 years and 2,536 aged >=35 years) and their newborns from all regions of Brazil.
finding: Advanced maternal age (AMA) was not associated with premature births (spontaneous or provider-initiated), but it was associated with a higher rate of provider-initiated early-term birth.
mod_finding: AMA did not increase the chance of premature births whether spontaneous or provider-initiated, but it was associated with a higher rate of provider-initiated early-term birth.
cross-section timing: Data was collected from puerperal women between 2011 and 2012.
